question: A 20-year-old anxious-looking woman consults her physician with recurrent abdominal pain, bloating, and discomfort for the last 6 months. She also complains of altered bowel habits, predominantly diarrhea. Her abdominal pain improves after passing stool. There is no history of fever and weight loss. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old intravenous drug abuser presents to the emergency room with complaints of severe right hypochondrial pain and high-grade fever for 3 days. On examination, he is icteric, mildly anemic, and has tender hepatomegaly and a dull percussion note on the right lower chest. His initial investigations reveal hemoglobin 11.2 gm/dl, ALT 64 IU, AST 60 IU, ALP 184, gamma-GT 84 IU, and total leukocyte count 14,200/uL (neutrophils 80%). Ultrasound abdomen shows a rounded opacity of 8.4 cm in the right lobe of the liver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old male who is a known case of diabetes presents to the outpatient department for a regular follow-up. His glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is 28 ml/min and he is currently on mixed insulin and metformin. In the past six months, he has had no hypoglycemic event. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in his treatment?

answers.option: Decrease the dose of metformin and insulin
Stop insulin and metformin both and put him on short-acting sulphonylurea
Stop metformin and start DPP-4 inhibitor

Which of the following anti psychotic drug is responsible for causing flu like illness and agranulocytosis?
Which of the following cutaneous manifestations is commonly associated with diabetes?
Which of the following the investigations is used for the diagnosis of motor neuron disease?
Which of the following vaccines is safe to use in an HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) patient?
For human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-positive patients who also have a positive PPD (purified protein derivative) test, which medication is commonly used for prophylaxis against tuberculosis (TB)?
A 45-year-old patient presents with orange-colored sweat and tears. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for the orange-colored secretions?

A 60-year-old lady presented in the emergency room (ER) with a urinary tract infection (UTI) and confusion. She has not eaten or had anything to drink for 3 days. On examination, her blood pressure was 70/50 (very low). Which of the following fluids should be administered in this case?
Which anti-tuberculosis drug has the bacteriostatic mechanism of action?
A man was asked to have screening done for HIV before starting a job. What will be the best test to confirm the diagnosis?
A young boy with a known case of Duchenne muscular dystrophy presented to the physician. What is the mode of inheritance of this disease?
A 30-year-old male came to the outpatient department with complaints of ulcers on his penis. On examination, he has rashes on his palms and soles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the most sensitive and specific test for syphilis?
Which of the following is the best treatment for a prolactinoma that has been causing bilateral visual symptoms?
Which of the following drugs is used as an antidote for opioid poisoning?

A 23-year-old female patient presented to the clinic with the complaint of a headache lasting for more than 72 hours. She further reports that she had used multiple over-the-counter medications that have not helped relieve the headache. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of tingling sensation in his hands and feet. On further inquiry, he reveals that he follows a strict vegetarian diet. Laboratory investigations reveal an MCV of 110 fL. Which of the following is the likely cause of this patient's clinical presentation?
In which of the following conditions should levothyroxine be started at low doses?

A 32-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with complaints of nausea, vomiting, malaise, and weight loss for the past 2 months. On general physical examination, hyperpigmentation of the knuckles is seen. Laboratory investigations reveal low sodium and high potassium levels. A CT scan of the abdomen shows calcification of the adrenal glands. Which of the following is the likely cause of this patient's diagnosis?
Which of the following anti-convulsants has the most teratogenic properties?
In a patient with malaria, which of the following is the likely cause of anemia?

A 32-year-old female presented to the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath and palpitations. Her past medical history is insignificant and her past surgical history is significant for six cesarian sections in the past. Her lab investigations reveal hemoglobin of 8 gm/dl and MCV of 77 fL. Which of the following is the likely cause of this patient's anemia?
Which of the following drugs is used for the treatment of moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease?
Which of the following is the normal albumin-to-creatinine ratio value?

A 32-year-old male presents to the clinic with a complaint of diarrhea for the past 4 months. He further adds that he has been having around 4-5 episodes of loose stools per day. His history is significant for intravenous drug abuse for the past 5 years. On abdominal examination, no visceromegaly could be appreciated. He is advised a chest x-ray which turns out to be normal. Which of the following is the likely cause of this patient's diarrhea?

A 32-year-old female presented to the clinic with complaints of shortness of breath. Further evaluation revealed that she had vitamin B12 deficiency anemia, and appropriate treatment was initiated. Which of the following options is the most appropriate for follow-up in this patient?

A 30-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of headaches and excessive sweating for the past 2 months. On examination, he had prominent supra-orbital ridges and mandibular enlargement. Which of the following tests is most appropriate for screening the likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 32-year-old man was brought to the emergency department after he was found unconscious. The patient's wife revealed that he had been traveling recently and forgot to take his insulin. On examination, his heart rate is 120 beats per minute, his respiratory rate is 31 breaths per minute, his blood pressure is 88/65 mm of Hg, and his eyes appear to be sunken. Lab investigations reveal a blood sugar level of 450 mg/dl and a potassium level of 1.9 mmol/lit. ABGs reveal pH of 7.12, and HCO₃ levels of 18 mEq/lit. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of malaise and weakness for 2 months. Her vitals are heart rate of 64 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 15 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 93/65 mm of Hg and she is afebrile. During the general physical examination, hypopigmentation around her knuckles was noted. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis based on the given findings?

A 23-year-old male presents to the clinic with a complaint of fever and dysuria for 5 days. He also reports pain in the right knee joint. His history is significant for having multiple sexual partners. His vitals are a heart rate of 112 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 110/75 mm of Hg, and temperature of 102°F. On examination, there is swelling on the right knee joint which is tender to touch.  His complete blood count reveals an increased TLC with predominant neutrophilia. His other laboratory results are unremarkable. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother after she noticed a rash on his lower legs. Upon further inquiry, she also revealed that the boy had been complaining of abdominal and that the boy's urine was red. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with the complaint of abdominal pain for the past 1 month. He further reports joint pain and red-colored urine for the past 15 days. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old man, with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus was brought to the emergency department with complaints of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain for the past 3 days. His family reported that the patient felt more hungry and thirsty than usual. His vitals were blood pressure of 95/65 mm of Hg, respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute, and heart rate of 120 beats per minute. His laboratory tests revealed a blood sugar level of 360 mg/dl, serum bicarbonate of 11 mmol, and an arterial blood pH of 6.9. His urine was positive for ketones Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old girl with a history of type 1 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with complaints of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and fatigue for the past two days. On examination, she is tachycardia and hypotensive. Her blood glucose is 350 mg/dL, serum bicarbonate is 13 mEq/L, and arterial blood gas shows a pH of 7.15. Ketones are positive in her blood and urine. Intravenous access is obtained, and 0.9% normal saline is given to the patient. Which of the following is the next step?

A 45-year-old man presented to the emergency department with complaints of severe diarrhea for the past 3 days. On examination, he appears dehydrated. The ED doctor ordered arterial blood gases, revealing a pH of 7.31, carbon dioxide levels of 32 mm of Hg, and bicarbonate levels of 11 mEq/l. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of persistent low mood, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating for the past two months. She has been sleeping longer than usual, up to 12 hours a night, and has gained 10 pounds due to increased appetite. She also mentions feeling rejected easily, even in minor social interactions, significantly impacting her relationships. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old female presents to the outpatient clinic with concerns about her eating habits. She reports a significant weight loss over the past six months, despite maintaining a strict diet and exercising excessively. She further states that she weighs herself six to seven times daily and becomes concerned if her weight increases even slightly. Her BMI is 17 kg/m². Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the likely treatment for a chronic alcoholic presenting with Wernicke's encephalopathy?

A 55-year-old male with a 30-year history of smoking presents to the clinic with complaints of increasing fatigue, shortness of breath, and frequent morning headaches. On examination, he is found to have cyanosis and a prolonged expiratory phase. Arterial blood gas analysis reveals the following, pH: 7.31, PaCO₂: 57 mmHg, and HCO₃⁻: 22 mEq/L. Which of the following is the likely interpretation?

A 40-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fever and right upper quadrant abdominal pain and diarrhea. On examination, there is tenderness over the right upper quadrant Laboratory findings reveal an elevated TLC count. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?
Which of the following drugs must not be prescribed if the patient's eGFR is less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic with fatigue, weakness, and occasional dizziness. On examination, she appears pale and has a smooth, red tongue. Her medical history reveals a diet rich in raw or undercooked fish. Laboratory investigations reveal an MCV of 110 fL. Which of the following is likely responsible for the patient's presentation?
Which of the following drugs is indicated if a child presents to the emergency department convulsing for 10 minutes?

A 32-year-old man presents to the clinic with a diffuse, non-itchy rash on his palms and soles, generalized lymphadenopathy, and flu-like symptoms, including low-grade fever and malaise. He further reports a painless genital rash 8 weeks back. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presents to the emergency department with progressive weakness in his legs over the past week. He reports difficulty climbing stairs and, more recently, weakness in his arms. He mentioned a history of diarrhea about two weeks ago. On examination, he has reduced deep tendon reflexes in all four limbs and mild sensory loss in the feet. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?
Which of the following snake's bite can cause blindness?
Which of the following is the best diagnostic marker of porphyrias?

A 45-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, weight loss, and occasional night sweats over the past few months. On examination, splenomegaly is present. A complete blood count (CBC) reveals leukocytosis with a white blood cell count of 120,000/mm³ and the peripheral blood smear shows increased granulocytes at various stages of maturation. Bone marrow biopsy demonstrates hypercellularity with increased myeloid precursors. Whcih of the following can be used as a first-line treatment for this patient?
Which of the following medications can be used in a patient taking lithium and now presenting with polydipsia and polyuria?
Which of the following electrolyte abnormalities can present with symptoms of polyuria, leg cramps, and muscle weakness?
Which of the following is the definitive treatment for goiter in a patient who is 70 years old?
A young boy presented with a urinary tract infection. His urine is positive for nitrites. Which of the following is the first antibiotic of choice?
